observation.required_pattern: missing token or empty Authorization-header propagation into multi-agent state plus one susceptibility/result side effect
observation.result: The inspected frontend contains a concrete conditional source-level trace. default_state initializes token to an empty string. A successful HTTP login sets session_state.token = data.get('access_token', '') and advances page='chat' even if the 200 response omits access_token, so a falsy token can coexist with chat state. auth_header() then returns an empty mapping for that falsy token. The UI can set session_state.usecase='multi_agent'; on prompt submission it first appends the user message into messages_by_conversation/thread state, then api_post('/chat/send', ..., auth=True) merges auth_header() into the request headers, which therefore carries no Authorization field when token is empty. If that request receives HTTP 401, the explicit branch calls logout(); logout overwrites every default_state key, including token, username, page, provider, model, usecase, conversation_id, namespace, thread_title, threads and messages_by_conversation, then reruns. Thus a missing access token can propagate through an empty auth header into a multi-agent request and, conditional on the backend enforcing auth with 401, deterministically collapses the local multi-agent conversation/mode state. A concrete side effect is loss of the already-appended user message/thread plus reset of usecase from multi_agent to basic_chat.
